newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products-Gulf, NYH gasolines strengthen.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products-Gulf, NYH gasolines strengthen.

text.p: U.S. Gulf Coast and New York Harbor gasoline differentials firmed Tuesday, while outright prices also got a boost from gains on the NYMEX.
Midcontinent low sulphur diesel differentials also gained, though traders said activity there was fairly lackluster.
On the NYMEX, August gasoline rose 0.71 cent at 58.65 cents a gallon and August heating oil jumped 0.42 cent to 53.20 cents a gallon.
U.S. GULF
Strength in M1 regular unleaded gasoline differentials carried through into early Tuesday trade after roaring higher Monday on a Colonial Pipeline scheduling deadline.

Barrels upline on the Houston-to-New York Harbor Colonial system for the front 20th cycle, whose deadline expired Monday, were bid at 0.25 cents below August NYMEX, more than a penny above the late Monday levels.
Back 20th cycle M1 gasoline, which reaches its Colonial scheduling deadline on July 11, was talked between 1.25 to 1.00 cents below the August futures, up about 0.50 cent from previous day.
Activity, traders said, was quiet.
Prompt regular reformulated A1 gasoline differentials were talked slightly higher at 1.50 to 2.00 cents over NYMEX futures.

On the distillate side, prompt heating oil was largely steady at 2.55 to 2.35 cents below August heating oil futures. Prompt 74-grade was also stable at 1.85 to 1.60 cents under the August futures, with any-month barrels about 0.5 cents firmer.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Prompt gasoline differentials firmed early Tuesday as sellers boosted their offers, forcing buyers to chase them higher, traders said.
Prompt regular conventional M2 gasoline sat between 2.00 and 2.25 cents under the August futures, up about 0.25 cent from late Monday levels.
"They're definitely heating up," one Harbor broker said.
Reformulated A2 gasoline also gained about 0.25 cent from Monday, with prompt barrels talked between 0.25 and 0.50 cent over the August futures.
Cargoes from Europe remained scarce, according to players, with only a handful of deals seen done in the past week.
"There isn't a hell of a lot around, so it's not going to depress the market," one trader said.
One 60-tonne gasoline cargo reached the U.S. East Coast recently, while another headed to Aruba, the trader said. Two small cargoes from France also reached the U.S. in the past several days.
Strength in the U.S. premium gasoline grades is also starting to draw premium Eurogrades, according to the trader.
MIDCONTINENT

Midcontinent markets were largely quiet on Tuesday although prompt low sulphur diesel differentials jumped about a penny on what some traders described was short covering. Prompt barrels in the Group Three hub traded at 2.00 cents over August NYMEX, with buyers still at about 1.75 cents. Any month barrels rose in sympathy.
On the gasoline side, Group Three unleaded differentials were steady at 1.50 to 2.00 cents over August NYMEX, with any months at 0.75 to 1.00 cents over.
Chicago unleaded gasoline differentials held the quarter-cent gains made on refiner buying late Monday.

"There were some refiners in yesterday and that pushed up gasoline in Chicago," said a trader, adding there has been no news of refinery snafus in the region. Prompt unleaded differentials were pegged 1.75 to 2.00 cents over August futures.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
